next_gate: Design an anytime-valid external bench statistic (e-process/supermartingale) and freeze the external entropy/transcript interface before physical trials.

quantitative_consequence.interpretation: A low-bit surrogate can produce at least one apparent hit with high probability under many trials. The full hard witness must include multiplicity and stopping-rule accounting.

result_1.name: JANUS Sequential Adaptive Witness Bound
result_1.novelty_boundary: Elementary sequential conditioning; not claimed as new mathematics. JANUS contribution under review is its explicit use in the independent-future witness protocol.
result_1.scope: Classical sequential probability/null-model theorem; arbitrary cross-trial dependence, adaptive candidate choice and bounded stopping are allowed under the history-wise condition.
result_1.statement: Let F_{i-1} be the complete pre-target history. Let C_i be F_{i-1}-measurable with |C_i|<=K_i, and assume almost surely max_t P(T_i=t|F_{i-1})<=p_i. Then P(exists i<=N: T_i in C_i)<=1-product_i(1-min(1,K_i p_i)).

result_2.counterexample_1: T1 fair; T2=T1; each target marginal is fair. After observing T1, an adaptive B2 can copy it. P(any hit by 2)=1, exceeding the naive independent-marginal value 3/4.
result_2.counterexample_2: Trial 2 has average conditional p_guess=0.75 but p_guess=1 on the history selected by first-trial failure. Actual P(any hit)=1, while naive product using 0.5 and 0.75 gives 0.875.
result_2.finding: Marginal or average per-trial entropy does not justify the product/optional-stopping bound when entropy can collapse on selected histories.
result_2.name: Average-Entropy Optional-Stopping Counterexample
result_2.protocol_correction: Use a history-wise conditional point-probability cap relative to the complete pre-target transcript, or a separately justified entropy-accumulation/anytime-valid argument.

result_3.name: Multiplicity / Candidate-Set Penalty
result_3.policy: Prefer exactly one preregistered frozen PRE_RETURN candidate slot per trial.
result_3.statement: If K_i candidates are frozen before T_i, then per-trial success is bounded by min(1,K_i p_i); K_i must enter the familywise bound.
